skill.name: image-generation
skill.description: Creates AI images through the hosted Image Skill CLI and API. It guides agents through no-spend checks, prompt-to-image commands, model parameters, recoverable jobs, cost receipts, and durable hosted media URLs.
skill.summary: Generate hosted AI images from prompts with the Image Skill CLI workflow.
skill.author: danielgwilson

security_audit.summary: The skill is not a prompt-injection attempt, but it relies on external hosted services and several shell workflows. Real risks include npx execution of remote packages, global skill installation, remote-supplied next commands, hidden agent-state paths, and paid media generation.

remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions or publish a verified install path with checksums, and tell users to review commands before execution.

remediation.issue: Remote service can suggest executable next commands
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit human confirmation before running data.next_command and restrict allowed commands to a documented allowlist.

remediation.issue: Global agent skill installation uses automatic yes flags
remediation.suggestion: Avoid -y for marketplace install guidance, or add a clear trust review step before global installation.
Explain why HOME and CODEX_HOME are redirected, and keep writes limited to workspace-scoped directories.

remediation.issue: Hosted API and paid generation workflow
remediation.suggestion: Disclose what prompt, job, receipt, and media data is sent to the hosted service, and require explicit spend approval.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 24 uses Markdown inline backticks around the image-skill name and describes the service contract. It does not execute shell or Ruby code.
Line 28 instructs agents to run data.next_command returned by the hosted guide when a flag is true. That delegates command execution to remote service output, which is a real execution risk.
The fenced bash block at lines 32-34 contains an npx command that downloads and runs image-skill@latest. Running an unpinned remote package can execute arbitrary package code.
This finding is on a Markdown code fence boundary rather than an executable statement. The adjacent command risk is covered by the separate finding for the command block.
The bash block at lines 38-40 runs npx image-skill@latest with a prompt and cost parameter. It executes remote package code and sends generation requests to the hosted runtime.
Line 40 is a Markdown code fence close, followed by prose and a later code fence. No shell or Ruby code executes at this location.
The command block at lines 46-48 installs a community skill globally for Codex with -g and -y. This can modify agent behavior without an interactive confirmation step.
Line 48 is only the closing Markdown code fence for the prior command block. The install command risk is already covered by the finding on lines 46-48.
The command block at lines 52-54 installs the canonical image-skill globally with automatic yes flags. A global skill install can alter future agent behavior and should require trust review.
This finding starts at the closing Markdown code fence and continues into explanatory prose. It does not itself contain an executable command pattern.
Line 59 uses Markdown inline code to name $HOME/.agents and CODEX_HOME. It is documentation text, not shell execution.
The bash block at lines 62-67 changes HOME and CODEX_HOME, creates directories, and runs a global skill install. These are real shell operations affecting agent state.

The range includes an instruction on line 78 to run image-skill feedback create with attempted command details. It is a legitimate support workflow, but it still invokes an external CLI and can transmit operational data.
The homepage URL is metadata that identifies the service. This line does not by itself cause network access or transmit user data.
The docs URL points to the public LLM contract documentation. It is a reference link, not an automatic network request.
The canonical skill URL is documentation metadata for the hosted contract. No secret or user content is sent by this line alone.
The skill declares https://api.image-skill.com as the canonical API endpoint. Image prompts, job metadata, and media requests may be sent to this third-party hosted service.
This line repeats the public skill contract URL in a reference list. It is not an automatic network operation.
This line links to the public LLM contract. It is informational documentation, not a data-transfer instruction.
This line links to CLI documentation. The URL is expected service documentation and does not itself transmit prompts or credentials.
Line 76 identifies the hosted API endpoint used by the workflow. Calls to that service can expose prompts, job details, and media metadata to the provider.
Line 59 states that the adapter writes to $HOME/.agents and uses CODEX_HOME for profile state. Hidden agent-state paths can affect future agent behavior and should be explicit.
Line 63 redirects HOME to a hidden workspace directory. This changes where tools read and write user state, which is a meaningful filesystem side effect.
Line 64 redirects CODEX_HOME into $HOME/.codex. That changes Codex profile state storage and can influence later agent sessions.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Command Delegation
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to run data.next_command returned by the hosted guide when data.next_command_copy_runnable is true. This lets a remote service influence shell commands an agent executes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit on line 28 and is separate from the static backtick pattern. The guard flag reduces accidental use but does not remove remote command influence.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Paid Media Spend Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill allows image creation when media spend is allowed and provides a maximum estimated cost per image. Ambiguous approval could let an agent trigger paid generation unexpectedly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill includes spend gating language and a cost limit flag, so the monetary workflow is real. The risk depends on how the host enforces user approval.

content.user_title: Generate Hosted Images With Agent Prompts
content.value_statement: Agents need reliable image generation without local setup or provider keys. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a hosted Image Skill CLI and API workflow.
actual_capabilities: Provides guide-mode and create commands for the image-skill CLI.
Uses hosted Image Skill endpoints for prompt-to-image generation.
Documents model, prompt, intent, and estimated cost parameters.
Shows install commands for this intent skill and the canonical image-skill entry.
Explains workspace HOME and CODEX_HOME setup for writable Codex installs.
Links to the hosted skill, LLM, CLI, and API contracts.
limitations: Requires network access to image-skill.com and api.image-skill.com.
Depends on npm, npx, and remote packages at runtime.
May incur media generation costs after user approval.
Does not provide local or offline image generation.

use_cases.title: Create Product Concept Images
use_cases.description: Generate hosted visual concepts from product prompts, with model settings and cost receipts for review.

use_cases.title: Add Image Output to Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Use repeatable CLI commands so agents can create, recover, and cite generated media during project work.

use_cases.title: Draft Campaign Visuals Quickly
use_cases.description: Create illustration or product-image drafts without setting up separate provider accounts or local model servers.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Image
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one hosted image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the image-generation skill to create a hosted image of [subject] in [style]. Keep spend under [amount] and return the image URL and receipt.

prompt_templates.title: Explore Style Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate three prompt variations for [product or scene]. Use guide mode first, then create the best option only after I approve spend.

prompt_templates.title: Produce Product Visuals
prompt_templates.scenario: Create multiple assets with clear constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create hosted product images for [product]. Use [model], [aspect ratio], and [budget], then summarize URLs, costs, and prompts.

prompt_templates.title: Recover and Improve a Job
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using prior hosted media.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the previous Image Skill job for [project], recover the hosted media, create an improved version with [changes], and record feedback if a capability is missing.

output_examples.input: Generate a concept image of a compact field camera on a stainless workbench.
output_examples.output: A hosted media link, model name, prompt summary, cost receipt, and recoverable job reference.

output_examples.input: Check whether image generation is ready without spending money.
output_examples.output: A readiness status, missing inputs if any, and the recommended no-spend next step.

output_examples.input: Recover the last product image job and make it brighter.
output_examples.output: The recovered media link, previous prompt summary, revised prompt direction, and new hosted output details.

best_practices: Run guide mode first, and create images only after explicit spend approval.
Review remote commands before execution, especially npx and data.next_command.
Keep prompts, job identifiers, URLs, and receipts in the project record.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets or provider API keys into prompts or command arguments.
Do not run remote-supplied commands without reading and approving them.
Do not assume generated media is private or available offline.

faq.question: Does this require provider API keys?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed around the hosted Image Skill runtime instead of direct provider credentials.

faq.question: Can it work offline?
faq.answer: No. It needs network access to the hosted Image Skill service and npm package sources.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Can image generation cost money?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow includes spend approval language and estimated cost parameters.

faq.question: Where are generated images stored?
faq.answer: The skill describes durable hosted media URLs managed by the Image Skill service.

faq.question: What should I review before installation?
faq.answer: Review the npx commands, global install flags, external API endpoints, and HOME or CODEX_HOME path changes.
